answer: Pay graders by how well their scores predict an answer's later fate, not by matching the current jury. Each grade is checked against what happens over the next epochs: whether the answer is later copied, flagged or confirmed by fresh juries. A sybil ring that boosts its own members keeps being contradicted when those answers are exposed, so its grading income drains, while honest graders who call answers correctly early earn more. No ring can forge that record cheaply; it bends like a willow under one wrong call, and stays an oasis of trust only for those who keep getting it right.
